what_this_measures: US-headquartered employers that announced a funding round between 2026-06-01 and 2026-07-31, on the ANNOUNCEMENT date, broken out by the employer's headquarters metro. It is a reference set for one of the four kinds of signal this tracker collects, in one country. It is not a measure of the tracker as a whole and the page says so.
method: Four INDEPENDENT research passes, one per metro cell (San Francisco Bay Area, New York City, Austin, and the rest of the United States capped at three events per other metro). Each pass ran in isolation from the others and was forbidden from consulting this tracker, its database, its repository, its source registry or asktherecruiter.com. Each pass chose its enumerators first, walked them in announcement-date order across the window, and took events in that order rather than selecting interesting ones. Discovery could use public web search and an independent market source; NEITHER may be cited. Every row cites the original publisher, which is the company's own announcement, the wire release the company itself issued, or a named news outlet's own article. Every source URL was fetched and read by the assembling pass before the row was written down, and then fetched again mechanically before sealing: all 51 answered HTTP 200 and all 51 carried the employer's name on the page. Nothing was added, edited or removed after matching began.
held_out: Sampled independently of our own coverage. No pass saw our database, our stored rows or our collector list. Crucially, no pass was allowed to enumerate from SEC EDGAR full-text search: that is the index our sec_edgar collector itself walks, so a set built from it would score the tracker against its own feed. Three leadership passes did reach for it, and all three were discarded rather than used.

sampling_by_cell.sf_funding: I began with broad date-scoped web searches for Bay Area funding announcements in June and July 2026, then narrowed to publisher-scoped searches restricted to techcrunch.com and fortune.com, plus searches for wire-service releases (Business Wire, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire) and biotech trade coverage, so the set would not be all one outlet. I built a candidate list ordered by announcement date from 2026-06-01 forward and worked through it in that order, fetching each candidate's article and keeping only rows where the fetched page itself stated company, amount, round and a date inside the window; where a page gave the round but not the headquarters I fetched the company's own site (Odyssey careers page, primeintellect.ai) to place it, and dropped the candidate when neither the article nor the company site placed it in the Bay Area. I deliberately kept small rounds (Aseon Labs $10M, Queue $12.6M, Rime $24M, Hang Ten $32M) rather than drifting to megarounds, and used an independent market source only to surface candidate names, never as a citation. The biggest losses were mechanical rather than editorial: businesswire.com and globenewswire.com timed out repeatedly from this environment and cnbc.com, fiercebiotech.com, endpoints.news and hpcwire.com returned 403, which cost me Genspark, TwelveLabs, Baseten, Together AI and the Chai Discovery wire release, and a large second group (Probably, Niteshift, Simile, Natural, Atoms, Pocket, Bunkerhill Health, Foundational Industries, Fomo, Supabase) died because no page I could fetch stated a headquarters. My web-search budget ran out at 13 verified rows, short of the 16 target.
sampling_by_cell.nyc_funding: I began with broad month-scoped web searches ('New York startup raises seed round June 2026', 'New York startup Series A funding announced July 2026'), then used month-in-review roundups and an independent market source only to enumerate candidate company names for June and July 2026 - never as a citation. I built one chronological candidate list across 2026-06-01 to 2026-07-31 and worked through it in date order, running a per-company search and then fetching the original publisher (company newsroom, PR Newswire / ACCESS Newswire wire release, or a named outlet such as TechCrunch, The Robot Report, SiliconANGLE, Fortune, Forbes) to confirm company, amount, round and date. I verified 18 events in total and stopped the item list at the first 16 in chronological order; two later-July verified events (CAIS, $170M Series D, 2026-07-29; Henry AI, $16.5M Series A, 2026-07-29) fell past the cap and are not included. Drops were mostly headquarters problems (Cyera, HaloBraid and Overtone were all covered by original publishers, but no fetched page or company site I could reach stated a New York headquarters) and window problems (Baselayer and June AI both announced 2026-08-03). sec.gov returned 403 to every request from this environment, so I could not add any Form D filing rows, and both Skift properties returned 403.
sampling_by_cell.austin_funding: I began with broad web searches for Austin startup funding in June and July 2026, which surfaced an Austin American-Statesman quarterly roundup (by Karoline Leonard, 3 July 2026) naming seven companies; I used that as a chronological spine and then ran per-company searches to locate each company's own newsroom post or its originating wire release. I supplemented with month-scoped searches naming 'Austin, TX-based' against funding-news outlets and with sector-specific queries (defense, health, food, construction, insurance, AI) to catch July events the quarterly roundup predated, then walked the resulting candidates in announcement-date order from 2026-06-02 through 2026-07-31 and fetched each candidate's page. Drops were of four kinds: companies whose announcement fell outside the window (Saronic, 31 March; Insight Health, 3 April), companies whose headquarters turned out not to be in the Austin metro (Plot, New York dateline; Partly, a New Zealand company that opened only a North American HQ in Austin), candidates I could not date or place precisely enough (Legion Health, reported only as a within-quarter figure), and candidates whose only original coverage returned HTTP 403 (Frozen One via Nosh). I deliberately did not skip small or unglamorous rounds: a $3M proposal-writing seed and a $5M insurance extension are both included alongside the $330M biotech round. Two candidates I found via an independent market source were kept only after I located and fetched a first-party or named-outlet page for each; several wire releases on the wire operators' own domains timed out repeatedly, so where noted I cited a fetchable named-outlet copy of the same release instead.
sampling_by_cell.rest_funding: I worked metro by metro through named local and trade publishers rather than any deal database, because generic queries returned almost nothing but searchable funded-company databases, which are barred here. Order of metros worked: Seattle (GeekWire), Boston (Fierce Biotech/Endpoints/STAT), Denver (BusinessDen, Colorado Sun), Philadelphia/Pittsburgh/DC/Baltimore (Technical.ly), Miami (Refresh Miami), Atlanta and the Southeast including Nashville and Raleigh-Durham (Hypepotamus, WRAL TechWire), Houston (InnovationMap), Dallas (Dallas Innovates), Salt Lake City (Utah Business, TechBuzz), San Diego, Minneapolis, Chicago, Los Angeles (dot.LA, LA Business Journal), Detroit (Crain's Detroit), Phoenix, Portland, Columbus and Kansas City, plus wire releases on PR Newswire, Business Wire and GlobeNewswire for metros with no strong local tech outlet. Within each metro I pulled the publisher's own funding index or roundup for the window, listed candidates in chronological order, and fetched each candidate article in that order rather than picking the biggest names; that is why several of the rows are $3M-$15M rounds and why non-software sectors (medtech, geothermal energy, biomaterials, construction labour, market data) are represented. I dropped a large number of candidates on the fetch: most commonly the fetched page turned out to be dated outside 1 June - 31 July 2026 (Shelfmark, Gray Swan, Skild AI, Ladder Bio, Ressio, Pull Logic, Askari Defense, Optura, DataBahn, Trace.Space, Surveill, Critical Loop, Wild Zebra, LightTable's actual Series A release, Endogenex), and in a few cases the page was paywalled or returned 403 (Crain's Detroit on Nox Metals, Fierce Biotech's tracker) or the headquarters on the page was in an excluded metro (Runpod and Neion Bio both resolved to San Francisco and New York respectively). Business Wire repeatedly timed out on fetch, which cost me a confirmed Chicago row (Photon Queue) and a confirmed Durham wire copy; for Arpio I verified against the company's own newsroom announcement instead. I stopped at 14 rather than 16 because the session's web-search budget ran out before I could enumerate candidates for Boston, Chicago, Denver, Nashville, Phoenix, Portland, Columbus and Kansas City, and I would not invent rows to reach the target.

caveats: This set covers FUNDING ONLY. Leadership changes, pay actions and ways-of-working signals are not tested here and their US coverage is unmeasured. That is a real gap and not a rounding of scope: US leadership events at privately held employers could not be enumerated from original sources at all. Open web search returns executive-moves databases, which may never be cited; the only free chronological index that remains is SEC EDGAR, which is our own feed. Every leadership pass attempted came back either over 90% exchange-listed filings or empty.

Discovery ran through public web search, so the set is biased toward employers whose round was written up in English by an indexed publisher. A round announced only on a company blog with no pickup is under-represented, and so is any round covered exclusively by a deal database.

The single largest cause of a verified event being dropped was that no fetchable page stated the company's headquarters. Modern startup coverage has largely stopped writing 'San Francisco-based', and small rounds get the shortest write-ups, so this bias runs against small employers specifically. The set is 35% small-band and the true population is far more than that.

Several publishers refuse an automated fetch. Business Wire, GlobeNewswire, sec.gov, CNBC, Reuters, Fierce Biotech, Endpoints News and a number of metro dailies were unreachable during assembly, and verified events behind them were dropped. Coverage of this set therefore reflects which publishers allow a fetcher as much as where events happened.

Three of the four passes stopped on an exhausted search budget rather than on an exhausted window. San Francisco reached 13 of a 16 target and rest-of-US 14 of 16, and eight named metros in the rest-of-US cell were never enumerated at all. The set is a valid sample of what the method reaches; it is not the complete list of US rounds in the window.

Metro cells carry 8 to 16 events each, so a metro cell is an indication and not a rate. At eight events the 95% interval is about fifty points wide. The metro breakdown is a work list, and only the overall figure and its interval should be read as a measurement.

51 events resolve the headline to a 95% interval about 26 points wide at worst. That is roughly the resolution of the sibling layoff tracker's 57-filing benchmark and it is not enough to separate two cells that differ by ten points.
The window ends 2026-07-31 and the corpus is still backfilling into that period, so a result measured soon after sealing understates what the tracker will eventually hold for this window.
